component: M=1 quantized decode split-K probe (lane matmul vs stock MLX qmv)

sources.used: Idea and split heuristic only, read from the PR description: split K across threadgroups when the N128 column-tile grid leaves cores idle (largest power of two S <= 8 with (N/128) x S <= 4 threadgroups per core and >= 256 inputs per partition; S = 1 above two tiles per core); S never depends on batch width. No code read or copied.

modifications: Probe only. mlx2's split-K is the lane matmul's in-threadgroup K slicing (runtime/lane/matmul.py split_k), not a cross-threadgroup split; stock MLX one-row qmv already launches N/8 threadgroups, so the idle-core premise of the splash tile does not carry over directly. The probe measures it rather than assuming.
qualification: no runtime change; probe artifacts only
